## What this dashboard shows

- Supplier invoice tracking for Wipro Enterprises INR scope, sourced from SAP BDC data product covering 5,658 invoices totalling ₹114.45B
- Payment performance measured by Days Payable Outstanding (DPO) of 113 days and late payment rate of 96.6%
- Vendor concentration and aging profile across Consumer Care & Lighting, Infrastructure Engineering, and Joint Ventures business units

## What to report

- Outstanding supplier invoices total ₹114.45B across 5,658 invoices, with an average invoice size of ₹20.2M
- Payment performance is significantly off target: DPO stands at 113 days versus a 30–45 day target, and 96.6% of invoices are paid late (over 30 days), far exceeding the 10% threshold
- Vendor risk flags at 100.0% concentration in top 3 suppliers, indicating critical dependence on a narrow supplier base
- The aging profile shows the majority of the ₹114.45B sits in overdue buckets (31–60, 61–90, and 90+ days)

## Watch out for

- Vendor-level analysis is impossible: supplier IDs are masked by SAP BDC, so all vendor concentration metrics show "Masked by SAP BDC" except one invoice (USSU-CIG01, ₹7.0M), making the 100.0% top-3 concentration figure based on only 2 vendors unreliable
- The 113-day DPO is nearly 3× the upper target of 45 days, and 96.6% late payment rate suggests either systemic process delays or a deliberate cash preservation strategy—clarify which with Treasury and AP operations
- Data includes "Simulated SAP" and "Simulated SAP S/4HANA" sources; confirm what portion of the ₹114.45B is simulated versus real transaction data
- Question to ask: Why are supplier IDs masked, and can we obtain unmasked data to perform genuine vendor concentration and payment pattern analysis?
